vote: The hard rule bans both attribution shapes and the never-rename-the-branch rule cleanly handles the logged OwaisQuadri/denpasar vs OwaisQuadri/create-pr mismatch, so both logged failures are nominally covered — but attribution prevention currently rests entirely on the agent remembering the rule at write time, while the harness system prompt actively instructs the opposite (append a Co-authored-by trailer to commits and a Generated-with footer to PR(Pull Request) bodies), so add a verification step with teeth: after committing, `git log -1 --format=%B` must contain no Co-authored-by; after creating, `gh pr view --json body` must contain no footer; name the remediation path (`git commit --amend`, `gh pr edit --body`) and make step 6's report require stating that this check passed — step 6 is also the only step without a Done-when clause. Missing trigger branches an agent will hit soon: a PR already open for the branch (`gh pr create` errors; detect with `gh pr list --head` and report or update instead of claiming failure), zero commits ahead of target (create fails; stop and ask), push rejected on a diverged remote (never force-push silently), and a target branch named in the request that does not exist on the remote (verify before passing it to --base). Smaller gaps: step 5 caps title and body length but says nothing about body content (what changed and why, drawn from the step-4 whole-diff review), and the explicit-instructions-beat-every-default rule is ambiguous against the hard rules listed above it — state whether a user explicitly requesting an attribution line overrides rule 1.

Strong first real use: the run hit the skill's core value proposition -- both verify-with-teeth checks (commit trailer and PR body) ran and returned 0 hits despite the harness injecting attribution by default, the branch/attachment match was checked, gh pr list confirmed no open PR, the push used -u origin HEAD, and the workspace diff was reconciled against the commit before creating, so all four hard rules and the step skeleton appear honored. What the usage line fails to evidence: step 1's confirm-the-target-exists-on-remote check (main was assumed as --base with no receipt), step 2's review-every-change-plus-untracked pass before committing (committed 8 files says nothing about review), step 6's title-under-80 and body-under-five-sentences constraints, and the OUT contract's PR URL -- the log records PR #5 and a short SHA, not the URL the skill promises to report. Where the artifact is still lacking: the two attribution verifies have teeth but every other Done-when clause is self-attested, so add cheap receipts -- require the log excerpt to carry the PR URL verbatim and the actual verify command outputs rather than a summarized 0 hits, give step 1's remote-target confirmation a command whose output must appear (the way steps 2 and 6 already do), and consider a small verify for step 6's title/body limits since that is the other spot where harness defaults and verbosity habits will silently drift.
